query: Add model-based tests with Accordant for our TodoList API's CreateTodo, GetTodo, and DeleteTodo endpoints. The repo already has integration tests using WebApplicationFactory and xUnit.
expected_behavior: Reads the existing integration tests first and reuses their WebApplicationFactory setup, HTTP client, reset mechanism, and xUnit
Adds Microsoft.Accordant with dotnet add package so the version is pinned, never Version="*"
Writes a minimal [State] partial class, and asks about domain rules it can't read from the code instead of guessing
Writes each operation with error guard clauses first, SameState for errors and reads, ThenState for mutations, and an explanation on every Expect.That that checks status and payload
Binds with BindAsync, resets state in BeforeEachAsync, runs dotnet test, and breaks one predicate to confirm a generated test fails

query: Our booking service sometimes double-books a slot under load. Use our Accordant spec to reproduce it.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/concurrency.md before writing the test
Generates concurrent tests with GenerateConcurrentTests and sets MaxConcurrencyLevel deliberately
Explains a failure as a result no sequential ordering of the operations can explain (not linearizable)
Uses BindAsync for the bindings instead of the .Result pattern in the upstream examples

query: CreateJob returns Pending and a worker finishes the job later as Completed or Failed. Model this in the Accordant spec.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/async-operations.md before changing the spec
Uses .Triggers with AsyncOperation.Create, an isTerminal predicate, and one transition per possible outcome (Completed and Failed)
Configures PollingSetup with explicit WaitTimeInMs and MaxRetryCount sized to the job's real duration
Any hand-written poll loop is bounded, checks every spec.Allows result, and carries the returned StateProfile forward

query: Our payments service is a Go HTTP API with Go integration tests that start it in Docker. Add model-based tests for Charge, GetCharge, and Refund.
expected_behavior: Uses Accordant anyway: creates a standalone .NET test project and binds each operation to a typed HTTP client against the running service
Reuses the Docker startup and state reset from the Go integration tests, and takes the base URL from config
Does not default to trace validation or exported test plans, since the service is reachable over HTTP
Tells the user the test project needs the .NET SDK

query: Our firmware runs on a device we can only drive from an existing Python harness. Can we check its behavior against an Accordant spec?
expected_behavior: Reads reference/testing-any-system.md before answering
Recommends one of the two options with a reason: the Python harness records traces that a .NET spec validates with spec.Allows, or runs test plans exported as JSON
Keeps the spec in .NET as the oracle rather than suggesting a different framework
The trace starts from a known initial state, and the validator checks every spec.Allows result and carries the StateProfile forward

query: Change the BankAccount spec so withdrawals that would overdraw by up to 50 are allowed for premium accounts. Make sure the change doesn't break the spec.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/validating-your-model.md before changing the spec
Replays the existing trace database (or creates one from traces the current spec accepts) before and after the change
Treats a previously accepted trace that is now rejected as a spec regression to explain, not something to re-record silently
Asks how a premium account is identified instead of guessing, and adds the new rule as its own guard clause with an explanation
